<!-- Generated by tools/cli-reference.py from `backdown update --help`. Edit the help in crates/backdown-cli (or the notes in the script) and run it again. -->


```text
backdown update [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

`--check`
: Only say whether there is one (exits 10 when there is); with --from, only verify the folder and change nothing.

`--refresh`
: Ask GitHub now instead of using today's answer.

`--rollback`
: Put back the version the last update replaced.

`--channel <CHANNEL>`
: stable or preview (default: as in Settings; previews while this is a preview).

`--json`
: Print it as JSON, for scripts.

`--from <FOLDER>`
: Install from FOLDER, without a network: it holds this system's release archive, SHA256SUMS.txt and SHA256SUMS.txt.sig, carried over from the release.

`--allow-unsigned` {preview}
: With --from: go ahead without SHA256SUMS.txt.sig. The checksums then show only that the files arrived whole, not that they're BackDown's.

`--allow-older` {preview}
: With --from: install it even if it isn't newer than this version.

Also takes the [global options](/docs/cli/#global-options) `--db` and `--local`.

## Good to know

Asks GitHub's public list of BackDown releases, only when you run it (or when Settings says to look once a day); the answer is kept for a day. Installing downloads this computer's archive and `SHA256SUMS.txt`, refuses unless the SHA-256 matches, checks the new program runs, keeps the old one in your data folder, swaps them and restarts the background service; if the new one doesn't start, the old one is put back. A copy installed by a package manager, an AppImage or Homebrew is updated that way instead, and it says so.

## Examples

```sh
# is there a newer version? (exits 10 when there is)
backdown update --check
# download it, check it against SHA256SUMS.txt and install it
backdown update
# put back the version the last update replaced
backdown update --rollback
```
